title: GPT-4o recognizes osteoarthritis from patient questionnaires in a selected cohort
summary: Researchers compared model-generated diagnoses from patient questionnaires with blinded clinician assessments. The primary results table records 85 correct GPT-4o diagnoses among 93 selected osteoarthritis cases. The study excluded non-osteoarthritis diagnoses, so it does not establish specificity, general triage accuracy or clinical benefit.
organization: University of Regensburg; Asklepios Klinikum Bad Abbach

evidence.tested: 115 questionnaires collected prospectively;93 clinician-confirmed osteoarthritis cases analyzed after exclusions. Clinicians were blinded to questionnaires; deidentified responses were subsequently submitted to pretrained models.
evidence.unknown: Source headline sensitivity 92.3% conflicts with Table 2 count85/93 (91.4%); represented result follows the explicit count. Negative diagnoses were excluded and one entirely symptom-incomplete questionnaire removed. GPT-4o helped design the questionnaire; prompts/repeated-generation details in supplements were uninspected. No locked deployment or outcome benefit.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o inferred diagnoses from patient-reported symptoms and history; its output was compared with independent clinician assessment.

source_review.scope: Actual primary cohort/model Methods, Results/Table2 and limitations in supported Chrome; source-front onlineDecember26,2024 versus2025collection distinguished. Internal headline/count discrepancy retained.
